body.heading: Starts are exciting, endings teach
paragraphs: Beginning a project is all possibility. Finishing one is where you learn judgement: what to cut, what to keep, and when to stop polishing and call it done.
If most of your projects stall at eighty percent, the missing skill is probably not talent. It is practice at endings, and endings can be practised on small things.

body.heading: Shrink the finish line
paragraphs: Choose projects you can complete in one sitting or one week: one short story, one song, one small shelf. Finish it fully, even if the result is rough.
Then let it be finished. Resist the urge to reopen it forever. A shelf of small, completed things builds more confidence than one endless masterpiece in progress.

takeaway: Pick things small enough to finish, and finish them all the way.
